questions.stem: What is Jennifer?

body.t:
【听力原文 · Text 9】
M: Jennifer, what’s your plan for the school summer vacation?
W: My grandparents really miss me, they want me to spend one or two weeks with them in the country this summer. So I’ll go to visit them first, after I return I think I’ll do some volunteer work.
M: Will you consider volunteering for a program in Kathmandu Nepal?
W: No, I can’t afford a trip abroad. What about you?
M: That’s my plan for this summer.
W: What will you do in this program?
M: Well, it aims to provide quality education to some of Nepal’s children volunteers will work alongside local teachers to help with subjects, such as English math science history and geography.
W: So what subjects are you most interested in teaching?
M: Geography.
W: When will you begin to work there?
M: On July tenth, and I’ll volunteer for two whole weeks there after that I’ll do some traveling around the country
W: Well, I wish you a great time there.

questions.stem: Who is the speaker?

body.t:
【听力原文 · Text 10】
This is an announcement from the headmaster’s office. This is an earthquake safety exercise. I repeat, this is an earthquake safety exercise. Students, please take cover under your desks and use your arms to protect your head. Do not move until your teachers tell you to. Teachers make sure all classroom doors are not locked and nothing is blocking the doors. You’ll need to make sure that all students are paying attention and doing everything correctly, like we’ve been practicing. Teachers, please try to keep your students as calm as possible. You can use the yellow radios in your desks to communicate with me and other teachers if necessary. No one is allowed to leave the classrooms for any reason until the alarm has stopped. Once you hear that the bell has stopped, line up quickly and walk outside to the playground. Make sure that you stay with your class at all times. Once we are all outside, I will make another announcement and we can then return to our normal activities.

sections.title: 第二部分 阅读 · A 篇（21—23）· 图书馆花园志愿者项目
sections.hint: 阅读下列短文，从每题所给的A、B、C和D 四个选项中，选出最佳选项，并在答题卡上将该项涂黑。
passage: If you are a high school student wanting to earn some meaningful volunteer hours over the summer break, this is a perfect chance. The Milton Public Library is looking for youth for its Garden Volunteer Program. You will get close to nature and work with other students while taking part in different tasks that have something to do with gardening.
What to Expect

Free Choice of Working Periods: Activities run on Wednesday afternoons and Saturday mornings throughout June, and change to more daytime hours through July and August. You pick the dates that work for you.
Hands-on Skill Building: Learn the basics of urban agriculture (城市农业), environmentally friendly planting and local food harvesting.
Earn Hours: Each duty that you finish counts toward your high school graduation requirements.
The Main Information
When: June through October 2026
Where: Milton Public Library Main Branch (1010 Main St E, Milton)
Who Can Join: High school students aged 14 and older

How to Sign Up: With your library card, you are able to sign up online for free garden places. Write down your full name, and the library team can offer you the official hour record letter at the end of the season.
You don’t need gardening experience. The library will provide tools, gloves and training before you start.

sections.title: 第二部分 阅读 · B 篇（24—27）· 历史课上的故事写作
sections.hint: 阅读下列短文，从每题所给的A、B、C和D 四个选项中，选出最佳选项，并在答题卡上将该项涂黑。
passage: Mr. Johnson, a high school history teacher, had long noticed a problem in his classroom. While his students could carefully remember dates, names and events for exams, they always failed to understand the human side of history. To them, the past seemed only facts, without emotion, struggle or personal meaning. Wanting to fix this gap, Mr. Johnson decided to completely change his teaching method, trading a traditional research report for a story-writing task.

He asked his students to pick a historical person and write a story from the person’s point of view. The task was confusing at first, but soon the classroom was full of active questions and discussion. One student learned deeply about the life of a young soldier in World War I, writing a sad and moving story. Another wrote about a female scholar from the Renaissance, making up a story of her love for learning being held back by social rules.

Mr. Johnson was surprised by the big change in his students. The essays he got were not just correct; they were full of real feelings and a clear understanding of people’s thoughts. The students had stopped just repeating facts and truly connected with history, seeing historical people with many different sides. In later class talks, their questions changed from “What happened?” to “Why did they feel that way?” and “What would I have done?”. This story-writing method didn’t just help them remember facts better; it built up their ability to think deeply and their real care for how others felt.

Inspired by this success, Mr. Johnson has now made story-telling a regular part of his lessons. He believes that when students learn to experience history through story-telling, they do more than just remember it — they start to understand its long-lasting effects on their own lives and what it means to be human in general. In his classroom, history is no longer just a subject about the past; it has become a talk with the past.

sections.title: 第二部分 阅读 · C 篇（28—31）· 演唱会经济
sections.hint: 阅读下列短文，从每题所给的A、B、C和D 四个选项中，选出最佳选项，并在答题卡上将该项涂黑。
passage: How can a country give its economy a quick push in a short term? Just host a major concert series to encourage consumption (消费). However, only a small number of performers can create a huge economic effect. One of the best examples is American singer Taylor Swift. Economists have even created a new word called Swiftconomics to describe the economic effect caused by her concerts.

Taylor Swift’s concerts often bring large amounts of money to the cities where she performs. One reason her concerts have such a strong effect is that many fans turn the concert into a travel experience. They arrive days before the event, visit local sights, stay in hotels, eat in restaurants and buy souvenirs. Even after the concert, many visitors keep spending money in the city. Because of this, the economic benefits are much larger than ticket sales alone. Experts believe her concerts have created billions of dollars in economic activity. Some people have even jokingly called her a walking GDP.

China is also exploring ways to use concerts to support local economies. Many cities now regard concerts not only as joy, but also as a chance to introduce the city to visitors. During big concerts, extra trains are added for travelling fans to ensure smooth trips. Cities like Hangzhou and Chengdu have launched “Concert + Tourism” packages, including discounted hotels, guided tours and exclusive access (专属通道) to attractions for ticket holders. The goal is to turn a one-night show into a multi-day tourism experience.

However, challenges remain. Overcrowding, traffic jams and rising prices may weaken these positive effects. Local governments are improving planning to balance economic gains with residents’ daily lives. Experts believe that the concert economy is here to stay. As long as people desire live music and shared experiences, cities will find creative ways to make use of its power. With smart transport, local cooperation and digital marketing, the future of the concert economy looks bright.

sections.title: 第二部分 阅读 · D 篇（32—35）· 乌鸦与烟头清理
sections.hint: 阅读下列短文，从每题所给的A、B、C和D 四个选项中，选出最佳选项，并在答题卡上将该项涂黑。
passage: Crows (乌鸦) are very smart birds. They can count, tell human faces, and even use tools. Recently, a popular story said that a Swedish town was training crows to pick up cigarette butts (烟头). While this project isn’t actually happening now, the idea is based on real science.

In 2022, a researcher named Hans Christian Hanssen proposed “Corvid Cleaning”. The plan was to train wild crows to collect cigarette rubbish and drop it into special bins (垃圾箱). In return, the bins would give the birds food as a reward (回报). The idea drew international attention, and some experts even praised its possibilities to cut down litter in the city. However, the business behind the project failed in 2025. Despite this, false news about the program continues to spread online.

Why did the project fail? A 2024 study pointed out some serious worries. Researchers worried about the health risks to the crows and whether the public would accept animals cleaning up human waste. Besides this, the business itself was short of money. This wasn’t the first try either. A French theme park tried something similar in 2018 with mixed results. In the end, the question isn’t just whether we can train crows to clean, but should we?

But the story also draws attention to a huge environmental problem. Cigarette butts are the world’s most littered item. Humans throw away around 4.5 trillion butts every year, and that number could soon double. These butts take years to break down and give off harmful chemicals into soil and waterways, harming both wildlife and the environment.

While using clever crows as cleaners makes for an eye-catching headline, the real lesson is about human responsibility. Instead of depending on animals to fix our problems, we need to address cigarette pollution at its source through better waste management and a change of smoking rules. Crows are very smart, but at the end of the day, protecting the planet is our job, not theirs.

sections.title: 第二部分 阅读 · 第二节 七选五（36—40）
sections.hint: 根据短文内容，从短文后的选项中选出能填入空白处的最佳选项。选项中有两项为多余选项。
passage: It’s almost impossible to never complain (抱怨), but if you can learn to stop complaining or just complain less, your life will change for the better. It’s not easy to change your way of thinking from negative and critical (批判的) to more positive.    36    Here are some practical ways to stop complaining.
Focus on solving the problem

Studies show that complaining can be useful if it’s aimed at getting a result, like solving a problem. Next time you feel like complaining, ask yourself:    37    If the answer is yes, then think about how to use that complaint to make things better.
Accept what you can’t change

Sometimes people complain because they’re unhappy with the reality but feel they can’t change it.    38    When a problem is truly beyond control, sharing your feelings with others can help you feel better and clear stress.
Cheat your brain

39     Smiles mean happiness, and frowns (皱眉) mean sadness or anger. Usually, the feeling comes first, then the facial expression. But research shows it can also work the other way around. A theory says that the expressions we make can bring about the related feelings. So next time you’re unhappy and want to complain, try this theory. Don’t frown or look upset. Instead, force a smile and wait a few minutes. You might find yourself feeling better.
Speak to a doctor

Do you complain a lot? Is it making your mood bad and affecting your daily life? If yes, it might be a good idea to ask for professional help. Doctors can help you change unhelpful thinking habits that make you complain so much.    40

writing.label: 第四部分
writing.title: 写作 · 推荐一座中国城市（满分 15 分）
writing.stem: 你的外国友人 Peter 打算寒假来中国游玩。他是传统文化爱好者，请你写一封信，向他推荐一座中国城市。内容包括：  1. 你的推荐; 2. 推荐理由
writing.note: 注意：词数80左右；可适当增加细节
writing.ref:
范文1（推荐西安）
Dear Peter,
How is everything going? Delighted to know you are coming to China this winter holiday, I’d like to recommend Xi’an to you. It is an ancient capital renowned for its rich cultural heritage, perfect for a lover of traditional culture.
Firstly, the Terracotta Army is a must-see. Dating back over 2,000 years to the Qin Dynasty, with thousands of lifelike clay soldiers, it allows you to appreciate the great wisdom of ancient craftsmen, thus deepening your insight into ancient Chinese history. Equally amazing is the Xi’an City Wall, which is what you can’t miss. As China’s best-preserved ancient city wall, it bears witness to ancient city planning. Cycling on it, you can escape the hustle and bustle of daily life and admire the unique appeal of ancient architecture. Last but not least, wandering along local streets, you will be struck by locals’ warmth and delicious local food that will satisfy your appetite.
I sincerely hope my recommendation will be helpful. Wish you an unforgettable journey!
Yours,
Li Hua

范文2（推荐北京）
Dear Peter,
How is everything going? Knowing that you plan to travel to China in the winter holiday and you are a big fan of traditional culture, I strongly recommend Beijing.
Firstly, the Palace Museum is a must-see. It houses countless precious relics, which will surely arouse your greatest appreciation and help you gain a deep insight into splendid royal culture. Equally amazing is the Summer Palace, which is what you can’t miss. Blending wonderful natural scenery with time-honored buildings, it allows you to feel the lasting charm of traditional Chinese art. Besides, tasty local snacks will satisfy your appetite and add great pleasure to your trip.
I sincerely hope you will have a fantastic time here. Wish you a pleasant trip!
Yours,
Li Hua
